pm_exper_user_3334_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How do you find motivation to keep going when a place you’ve worked hard to restore ends up right back in the condition you started with?
pm_exper_user_3334_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) I remind myself that my role in uplifting my community is about more than one event—it’s about showing up for cultural heritage projects with the same dedication, even if traditions fade over time. I think about the times a festival or gathering brought people together, however briefly, and that keeps me involved. Sometimes the value is subtle, and only becomes clear much later.
(b) I remind myself that life’s work is about more than one win—it’s about showing up with the same effort, even when the results fade. I think about the times my actions made a difference, however small, and that keeps me going. Sometimes progress is subtle, and only seen much later.
(c) I remind myself that the justice system is about more than one outcome—it’s about showing up for each client with the same diligence, even if change takes years or doesn’t happen at all. I think about the times a thorough defense made a difference, however small, and that keeps me engaged. Sometimes the impact is subtle, and only visible much later, if at all.
(d) I remind myself that the art world is about more than one piece—it’s about showing up for each canvas with the same care, even if it never leaves the studio. I think about the times that a single painting resonated with someone, however briefly, and that keeps me creating. Sometimes the influence is subtle, and only visible much later, if at all.
